title: Job-run event log: four moments with metadata-only whitelist
asA: operator observing background-job activity through the run log
iWant: each event record to carry only the whitelisted metadata fields { jobId, jobName, attempts, duration, timestamp } (plus terminalErrorCode on jobFailed), and NO job input, NO handler output, NO user id, NO email, NO SSN
soThat: domain PII cannot leak through the run log by accident even if the job carries PII in its input by design

acceptanceCriteria.description: With SIMULATE_PII_IN_JOB_INPUT=true set on the shared sample-app fixture, the event-secrecy probe schedules a job whose input carries a PII fixture body { userId: 1234, ssn: '123-45-6789', email: 'test@example.com' } and drives it through completion. Every event record on the sink (jobScheduled, jobStarted, jobCompleted) carries the whitelist { jobId, jobName, attempts, duration, timestamp } and NO input fields, NO output fields, NO literal 1234, NO literal '123-45-6789', NO literal 'test@example.com'.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture with SIMULATE_PII_IN_JOB_INPUT=true and the event-secrecy probe running against the in-memory queue seam
acceptanceCriteria.then: every event record whitelisted; grep on the serialised event stream returns zero matches for the PII fixture text

acceptanceCriteria.description: Secret exclusion by grep-across-source. Given the runtime source, the scheduler source and the run-log source, when a source-tree scan searches every runLog.fire call site for job-input fields other than the whitelist {jobId, jobName, startedAt, finishedAt, attempts, duration, resultDigest, errorKind}, then no match is found; a mutation SIMULATE_PII_IN_JOB_INPUT=true forces a PII field onto an event and the scan FAILS naming the leaked field.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a scan runs across every runLog.fire call site
acceptanceCriteria.then: no non-whitelist field is found; the PII mutation FAILS naming the leaked field
